subject: System Design
title: Typeahead vs Fuzzy Search
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Typeahead vs Fuzzy Search.

hook.text: You type 'javscript' — a typo. Smart search still returns results for 'JavaScript.' That's fuzzy matching at work.

buildup.text: Typeahead matches exact prefixes: type 'jav' to see 'JavaScript.' Fuzzy search tolerates errors and misspellings.

discovery.text: Fuzzy search uses edit distance: how many changes turn the query into a known word. 'javscript' is 1 edit away.

twist.text: Fuzzy matching is expensive. Checking edit distance against millions of words requires clever indexing like n-grams.

climax.text: Great search combines both: typeahead for fast prefix matching, fuzzy for typo tolerance. Users don't even notice.

punchline.text: Prefix match for speed, fuzzy match for typo tolerance.

quiz.question: What is edit distance in fuzzy search?
options: The number of character changes needed to transform one word into another
The time to process a search query
